Myopic

/my-OP-ik/ - the stress falls on OP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Myopic means lacking foresight; focused only on the short term.

Skipping breakfast to cram five more vocabulary words is myopic — the gain shows up now, the blur arrives by the second hour of the exam.

Worked Example

The eighty-dollar roof patch waited all autumn. There was always a nearer use for eighty dollars — a concert, a brake light, a weekend — and the stain on the ceiling grew politely, an inch a month, until a February thaw brought the bedroom ceiling down. The contractor's bill was four thousand dollars. Every decision along the way had felt, at the time, like thrift.

Myopic is the exact word because each choice lacked foresight — focused only on the short term, the word's borrowed meaning from nearsightedness: near things sharp, far things blurred. A myopic decision isn't stupid and isn't reckless; next month simply crowds next year out of focus. The bill for the far blur always arrives.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shortsighted: the plain English twin — near gains over far costs

blinkered: unable to see outside one narrow view

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

farsighted: plans for what is coming long before it comes

forward-thinking: builds today with tomorrow already priced in

Where it sits · how far ahead the vision reaches — narrow → myopic → blind

narrow vs. myopic: A narrow view leaves things out to the sides; a myopic one loses everything past the near term.

blind vs. myopic: Blind goes past myopic — the nearsighted planner still sees this quarter clearly; the blind one sees nothing coming from any distance.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — my

Root — my: to shut, to close (Greek myein)

Root — op

Root — op: eye (Greek ops)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: My- (to shut, Greek myein) + op- (eye, Greek ops) + -ic (relating to) = shut-eyed. Greek doctors watched the nearsighted squint — half-shutting their eyes to sharpen the distance — and named the condition after the squint itself. English borrowed the diagnosis, then aimed it at planning: the myopic decision squints at next year and still can't make it out.

Use the root in a new word: optician

Use the root in a new word: optician: The optician had my new lenses ground and fitted before the weekend.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / critical

Myopic is the critic's word for decisions that can't see past the near term — policies, budgets, strategies. It is not stupidity: this unit's inept fails for lack of skill, but a myopic plan may be executed brilliantly toward a horizon two feet away. Its true opposite in this unit is judicious, which weighs the far term as heavily as the near. Shortsighted says the same thing in plainer clothes.
